subtitle: Rao Daljit, Sultan Mahmud, and the Broken Road to Delhi

panels.shot: epic split composition, half showing desert fortress walls, half showing burning city skyline behind war elephants
panels.action: Rao Daljit stands grim upon Bhatner’s sandstone ramparts as dust-darkened riders approach, while in the far haze another vision shows Sultan Mahmud Tughlaq framed by Delhi’s looming walls and lines of armoured elephants before fires on the horizon.

dialogue.text: In 1398, as Timur rode for Delhi, Rao Daljit and Sultan Mahmud stood on a road where courage could not stop catastrophe, yet still demanded to be remembered.

i18n.hi: १३९८ में, जब तैमूर दिल्ली की तरफ़ बढ़ा, राव दलजीत और सुल्तान महमूद उस राह पर खड़े थे जहाँ हिम्मत तबाही रोक न सकी, पर याद रहने की ज़िद कर गई।

panels.shot: wide aerial of north India plains with route traced from Kabul to the Sutlej and down towards Bhatner and Delhi
panels.action: A map-like sweep shows Timur’s columns snaking from the northwest through the Punjab plains, smoke rising from sacked towns, while a small marker glows over the desert stronghold of Bhatner and another over the distant sprawl of Delhi.

dialogue.text: Timur crossed the Indus like a moving camp of iron, his own chroniclers boasting of towns broken, prisoners taken, and a road of fear leading toward Delhi.

i18n.hi: तैमूर लोहा बनी चलती छावनी सा सिंधु पार कर आया, उसके इतिहासकार शहरों के उजड़ने, क़ैदियों की लदी कतारों और दिल्ली तक फैली दहशत की राह पर फ़ख्र करते रहे।

panels.shot: medium shot inside Bhatner fort courtyard, low-angle on Rao Daljit
panels.action: Rao Daljit, Rajput lord of Bhatner, stands in mail and turban in a sun-baked courtyard, gesturing to thick mud-brick and stone walls as desert warriors gather around him, camels and horses tethered in the background.

dialogue.text: On the Ghaggar’s edge stood Bhatner, a desert fort long watching the frontier, where Rao Daljit chose stone walls over flight as Timur’s advance drew nearer.

i18n.hi: घग्गर के किनारे था भटनेर, सरहद पर सदियों से खड़ा रेगिस्तानी क़िला, जहाँ तैमूरी खतरा नज़दीक आते ही राव दलजीत ने भागने से ज़्यादा पत्थर की दीवारें चुनीं।

panels.shot: close-up on Rao Daljit’s face, half-lit, eyes focused outward
panels.action: Rao Daljit leans over the parapet, jaw set, eyes narrowed at a distant cloud of dust on the horizon, his hand clenched on the hilt of his sword as wind tugs his sash.

dialogue.speaker: Rao Daljit
dialogue.text: If the gate is opened once, no man closes it again.

i18n.hi: एक बार फाटक खुल जाए, फिर कोई उसे बंद नहीं कर सकता।

panels.shot: wide shot from behind the battlements, showing Timurid vanguard arriving
panels.action: From the shadowed battlements, defenders look down on distant Timurid horsemen fanning out, their banners sharp against the pale desert, siege lines beginning to form around Bhatner’s low, thick walls.

dialogue.text: Sharaf al-Din Yazdi’s Zafarnama names Bhatner as a fortress that dared to bar Timur’s way, its garrison answering steppe horsemen with stone and resolve.

i18n.hi: शरफ़ुद्दीन यज़्दी की ज़फ़रनामा भटनेर को उस क़िले के नाम से लिखती है जिसने तैमूर की राह रोकी, जिसकी फ़ौज ने घुड़सवारों का जवाब पत्थर और जिद से दिया।

panels.shot: dynamic mid-shot of defenders on the wall in action
panels.action: Rao Daljit signals as defenders haul up heavy stones and fire arrows from crenellations, while outside Timurid soldiers raise ladders and roll siege engines toward the battered but unbreached walls.

dialogue.text: For days, perhaps weeks, according to the Persian chronicle, Bhatner’s walls drank the weight of arrows, stones, and fire, its lord refusing the summons to surrender.

i18n.hi: फ़ारसी तवारीख़ के मुताबिक़, दिनों क्या हफ़्तों तक भटनेर की दीवारें तीरों, पत्थरों और आग का बोझ पीती रहीं, उसका सरदार झुकने और आत्मसमर्पण से इनकार करता रहा।

panels.shot: low-angle close on a crumbling wall section, dust and debris frozen mid-fall
panels.action: A section of Bhatner’s wall buckles under impact, dust pluming as masonry slumps, defenders staggering back while Timurid troops surge toward the breach with shields raised.

dialogue.text: But Timur’s armies brought numbers, engines, and patience; Yazdi claims the fort fell after relentless assault, its capture praised as a gate opened toward the heartland.

i18n.hi: पर तैमूर की फ़ौजें संख्या, औज़ार और सब्र लेकर आईं; यज़्दी लिखता है कि बे-दर-ओ-पेकर हमलों के बाद क़िला गिरा, उसकी फ़तह को देहात का दरवाज़ा खुलना बताया गया।

panels.shot: somber medium shot of Rao Daljit in chains among other captives
panels.action: Rao Daljit stands bound among lines of captured soldiers and civilians outside the ruined fort, Timurid guards on horseback watching as smoke rises from the devastated town behind them.

dialogue.text: Later traditions remember Rao Daljit as fallen in the defence; the Timurid record, focused on Timur’s glory, lingers instead on plunder taken and captives driven on toward Delhi.

i18n.hi: बाद की परंपरा में राव दलजीत भटनेर की आख़िरी लड़ाई में शहीद याद होते हैं; तैमूरी रिकार्ड में, जो तैमूर की शान पर टिका है, बस लूट और दिल्ली की तरफ़ हाँके गए क़ैदियों का ज़िक्र ठहरता है।

panels.shot: transition wide shot of marching column of prisoners and troops on dusty road
panels.action: A long, weary column of prisoners shuffles along under guard beside armoured cavalry, the winter sun low over the plains as the distant silhouette of Delhi’s domes and minarets begins to form on the horizon.

dialogue.text: From Bhatner and other towns, chains of prisoners stretched behind the army; the Malfuzat-i-Timuri tradition speaks of captives counted not in hundreds, but in countless bundles of fear.

i18n.hi: भटनेर और दूसरे शहरों से क़ैदियों की ज़ंजीरें फ़ौज के पीछे दूर तक खिंच गईं; मल्फ़ूज़ात-ए-तैमूरी में गिनती सैंकड़ों नहीं, बल्कि ख़ौफ़ की अनगिनत गाठों में बताई गई।

panels.shot: interior medium shot of Sultan Mahmud Tughlaq in Delhi court
panels.action: Inside a dim Durbar hall in Delhi, Sultan Mahmud Tughlaq sits on a modest throne, features youthful and tense, as weary nobles and commanders stand in debate around him beneath peeling frescoes of past glories.

dialogue.text: In Delhi sat Sultan Mahmud Shah Tughlaq, heir of a weakening house, his court riven by factions, his treasury strained, yet his city still the richest jewel on the Yamuna.

i18n.hi: दिल्ली में बैठा था सुल्तान महमूद शाह तुग़लक़, ढलती सल्तनत का वारिस, दरबार गुटों में बँटा, ख़ज़ाना थका, पर यमुना किनारे उसकी नगरी अब भी सबसे चमकता रत्न थी।

panels.shot: close-up on Mahmud’s hand over a map, candles flickering
panels.action: Mahmud leans over a rough map spread on a low table, his hand resting near a charcoal mark labeled for Delhi, while small counters shaped like elephants and horsemen cluster at its edge.

dialogue.speaker: Mahmud Tughlaq
dialogue.text: If we do not meet him outside the city, we fight in its streets.

i18n.hi: अगर हम उसे शहर के बाहर न रोकें, तो लड़ाई गलियों में होगी।

panels.shot: sunrise wide shot of Delhi’s field army assembling with elephants
panels.action: At dawn outside Delhi’s walls, ranks of foot soldiers form up alongside towering war elephants in armour, mahouts perched high, as Mahmud Tughlaq rides his horse along the line, cloak whipping in the cold wind.

dialogue.text: The chroniclers agree: Delhi’s defenders marched out with elephants and men to meet Timur near the city, hoping weight and fear of those beasts would break the invader’s resolve.

i18n.hi: इतिहासकार मानते हैं: दिल्ली के रक्षक हाथी और फ़ौज लेकर शहर से बाहर तैमूर से भिड़ने निकले, उम्मीद थी कि उन जानवरों का बोझ और खौफ़ हमलावरों का दिल तोड़ देगा।

panels.shot: mid shot focusing on war elephants with towers and archers
panels.action: Armoured elephants stand in a line, metal plates glinting, with small wooden howdahs atop them where archers peer toward the enemy, dust hanging in the air before battle.

dialogue.text: Timur’s own accounts describe his alarm at the elephants and his decision to counter them not by retreat, but by using wagons, trenches, and fire to blunt their charge.

i18n.hi: तैमूर अपने बयान में हाथियों से दहशत और पीछे हटने के बजाय गाड़ियों, खाइयों और आग से उनके हमले को तोड़ने का फ़ैसला लिखता है।

panels.shot: dramatic wide shot of opposing armies facing off, Delhi’s elephants vs Timurid lines
panels.action: Across a flat field, Delhi’s army with its elephant line faces the disciplined Timurid ranks, wagons lashed together, horse archers ready, the two forces frozen in a heartbeat before the clash.

dialogue.text: Near modern-day Delhi, Timur wrote of anchoring his army behind carts and trenches, of ordering fires and camels to panic the elephants, turning the defenders’ greatest strength into confusion.

i18n.hi: आज की दिल्ली के पास, तैमूर लिखता है कि उसने फ़ौज को गाड़ियों और खाइयों के पीछे जाम दिया, आगों और ऊँटों का हुक्म दिया ताकि हाथी घबरा जाएँ और रक्षकों की सबसे बड़ी ताक़त अफ़रातफ़री बन जाए।

panels.shot: chaotic medium shot showing elephants turning back into Delhi’s lines
panels.action: Amid swirling dust, an elephant, eyes wide with fear, twists away from a wall of smoke and fire, crashing sideways into Delhi’s own infantry who scatter in disarray under its massive bulk.

dialogue.text: Persian narratives, eager to magnify Timur’s skill, describe how smoke and missiles sent the elephants back upon their own men; Delhi’s line broke, and with it the last field defence of the Tughlaqs.

i18n.hi: फ़ारसी रिवायतें, जो तैमूर के हुनर को बढ़ा-चढ़ाकर कहती हैं, लिखती हैं कि धुएँ और गोलाबारी ने हाथियों को पलटा दिया, वे अपने ही सिपाहियों पर चढ़ गए; दिल्ली की पंक्ति टूटी और साथ में तुग़लक़ों की आख़िरी मैदानी रुकावट भी।

panels.shot: somber mid shot of Mahmud retreating toward the city gate
panels.action: Sultan Mahmud, face drawn, rides back toward Delhi’s gate amid a stream of retreating soldiers, glancing once over his shoulder as Timurid standards begin to push closer across the field.

dialogue.text: Defeat did not erase the attempt; yet the sources agree that Mahmud’s army broke and fled for the walls, leaving the city to face an enemy who claimed divine favour in victory.

i18n.hi: हार ने कोशिश मिटा नहीं दी; फिर भी सभी बयान मानते हैं कि महमूद की फ़ौज टूटी और भागकर दीवारों पर जा सिमटी, शहर को उस दुश्मन के हवाले छोड़ते हुए जो अपनी फ़तह को खुदाई मदद बताता था।

panels.shot: grim wide shot of prisoners herded together in a field camp outside Delhi
panels.action: In a bleak camp near the Yamuna, masses of prisoners sit or kneel under guard, the tents of the Timurid host stretching away behind them, Delhi’s domes faint in the distance under a grey sky.

dialogue.text: Here, the record falls hardest: both Yazdi and the Malfuzat tradition speak of Timur ordering the killing of his many prisoners before the battle for Delhi, claiming fear of revolt in his rear.

i18n.hi: यहीं रिकार्ड सबसे भारी हो जाता है: यज़्दी और मल्फ़ूज़ात दोनों लिखते हैं कि दिल्ली की जंग से पहले तैमूर ने पीछे बंधे हज़ारों क़ैदियों को मरवा देने का हुक्म दिया, बहाना था पीछे बगावत का डर।

panels.shot: close-up on a Timurid officer’s stern face, prisoners blurred behind
panels.action: A Timurid officer’s face is shown in hard profile as he looks over the lines of bound men, his expression rigid, while prisoners crouch in the blurred background under the watch of armed guards.

dialogue.text: The chronicles give a vast round figure for the slain, likely a symbol of enormity rather than a count, but in both friendly and later accounts, the massacre itself stands attested.

i18n.hi: तवारीख़ मारे गए लोगों की गिनती एक बहुत बड़ी, गोल संख्या में देती हैं, शायद बस उसकी हैवानियत का निशान, पर दोस्त और दुश्मन दोनों के बयान में क़त्लेआम खुद दर्ज रहा।

panels.shot: majestic yet ominous wide shot of Timur’s forces entering Delhi with Mahmud absent from the walls
panels.action: Timurid soldiers march through an opened gate into Delhi, banners unfurled, while the city’s walls stand strangely quiet, no sign of Mahmud on the parapets as ordinary townsfolk watch from doorways or slip away into alleys.

dialogue.text: Timur entered Delhi in December 1398; Yazdi portrays the sultan absent and the city subdued, the conqueror holding court in a capital that had once commanded the plains he now traversed.

i18n.hi: तैमूर दिसंबर १३९८ में दिल्ली में दाख़िल हुआ; यज़्दी सुल्तान को ग़ायब और शहर को झुका हुआ दिखाता है, विजेता उसी राजधानी में दरबार लगाते हुए जो कभी इन मैदानी इलाक़ों पर हुक्म चलाती थी जिन पर अब वह निकल पड़ा था।

panels.shot: medium interior shot of Delhi residents in narrow lane as distant turmoil builds
panels.action: Within a cramped Delhi lane, merchants shutter shops and families clutch bundles, glancing toward the faint echo of distant shouts, while foreign soldiers move along a larger street beyond.

dialogue.text: Yet occupation did not stay quiet; the sources describe unrest breaking out in Delhi, with townspeople or remaining soldiers clashing with Timurid troops, their anger and fear igniting a new storm.

i18n.hi: पर क़ब्ज़ा चुप नहीं रहा; रिवायतें लिखती हैं कि दिल्ली में फिर ख़लबली भड़की, शहरियों या बचे सिपाहियों की तकरार तैमूरी सैनीकों से हुई, उनका ग़ुस्सा और डर नयी आँधी बन उठा।

panels.shot: dark, wide shot of Delhi quarter with fires in distance, people fleeing
panels.action: Night cloaks a quarter of Delhi as firelight flares in the distance; silhouettes of people hurry through shadowed streets carrying children and bundles, while armoured figures move at crossroads.

dialogue.text: In answer to the uprising, Yazdi and other Persian accounts describe Timur ordering a qatl-i-am, a general killing in the city, and the taking of artisans and captives for deportation.

i18n.hi: इस बगावत के जवाब में, यज़्दी और दूसरे फ़ारसी बयान लिखते हैं कि तैमूर ने क़त्ल-ए-आम का हुक्म दिया, शहर में आम मारकाट और कारीगरों व क़ैदियों को उठा ले जाने की तैयारी हुई।

panels.shot: somber medium shot of artisans being selected and led away from ruined workshops
panels.action: In a partially ruined bazaar, Timurid officers point out skilled artisans—metalworkers, weavers, architects—who gather their tools under guard as smoke drifts through broken arches.

dialogue.text: The chronicles dwell on the artisans chosen and sent to Samarkand, a flow of skill drawn from Delhi’s ruin, while leaving the numbers of dead in the city itself shrouded in vast, uncertain claims.

i18n.hi: तवारीख़ उन कारीगरों पर रुकती हैं जिन्हें चुनकर समरकंद भेजा गया, हुनर की धारा जो दिल्ली की बर्बादी से खींची गई, जबकि शहर में मारे गए लोगों की गिनती धुँधले, बेहिसाब दावों में छोड़ दी गई।

panels.shot: wide shot of Timur’s army leaving Delhi, city scarred behind
panels.action: A long line of Timurid troops, carts, and chained captives moves away from Delhi under a pale sky; the city behind shows charred roofs, broken domes, and a haze of lingering smoke over the Yamuna.

dialogue.text: When Timur left, he carried wealth, captives, and stories of triumph; modern historians like Irfan Habib and Justin Marozzi instead trace the economic wound left on north India’s heart.

i18n.hi: जब तैमूर लौटा, वो दौलत, क़ैदी और फ़तह की कहानी ले गया; आज के इतिहासकार जैसे इरफ़ान हबीब और जस्टिन मैरोज़ी इसके बदले उत्तर भारत के दिल पर लगी आर्थिक चोट का पीछा करते हैं।

panels.shot: quiet mid shot of Mahmud Tughlaq in a modest camp outside ruined Delhi later
panels.action: Later, Sultan Mahmud sits in a small tented camp outside a scarred Delhi skyline, his robe plain, head bowed, a few loyal retainers standing at a respectful distance in the dusk.

dialogue.text: Mahmud returned to a broken capital; the Tughlaq line, already weakened, staggered on amid rivals and factions, its authority now a shadow over a city that had seen sack and slaughter.

i18n.hi: महमूद एक टूटी राजधानी में लौटा; तुग़लक़ ख़ानदान, जो पहले ही कमज़ोर था, अब प्रतिद्वंद्वियों और गुटों के बीच लड़खड़ाता रहा, उसकी हुकूमत उस शहर पर बस एक साया रह गई जिसने अभी-अभी लूट और क़त्ल देखा था।

panels.shot: reflective wide shot juxtaposing ghostly images of Bhatner’s walls and Delhi’s skyline
panels.action: In a composite vision, the battered walls of Bhatner rise on one side and Delhi’s scarred domes on the other, with faint, ghostlike figures of Rao Daljit and Mahmud Tughlaq facing opposite horizons under the same pale sky.

dialogue.text: From Bhatner’s last stand to Delhi’s fallen throne, the chronicles remember Timur’s victory; yet in their margins survive the shapes of those who resisted, showing that honour and disaster can share the same page.

i18n.hi: भटनेर की आख़िरी जंग से दिल्ली के गिरे तख़्त तक, तवारीख़ तैमूर की फ़तह लिखती हैं; पर उनकी हाशियों में उन सबके नक़्श भी बचे हैं जिन्होंने मुक़ाबला किया, दिखाते हुए कि इज़्ज़त और तबाही एक ही सफ़े पर साथ रह सकती हैं।

title_i18n.hi: भटनेर से दिल्ली — तैमूर के ख़िलाफ़

subtitle_i18n.en: Rao Daljit, Sultan Mahmud, and the Broken Road to Delhi
subtitle_i18n.hi: राव दलजीत, सुल्तान महमूद, और दिल्ली तक टूटा रास्ता
